citation.title: What is access? A discussion of the definition and measurement of interest group access
citation.type: journal article (only abstract, notes and reference list available in the saved page)

question: Abstract: how the concept of access is defined and measured in interest group research, and how operationalisations based on the authors' proposed definition compare with major alternatives in the literature.
method: Abstract: "On the basis of a review of this literature" (review of the interest group access literature), then a comparison of operationalisations. No further detail available.

definitions.definition: Instances where a group has entered a political arena (parliament, administration or media) by passing a threshold controlled by relevant gatekeepers (politicians, civil servants or journalists).
definitions.quote: We propose to define access as instances where a group has entered a political arena (parliament, administration, or media) passing a threshold controlled by relevant gatekeepers (politicians, civil servants, or journalists).

definitions.definition: Access does not guarantee influence but is customarily seen as a step towards it; groups with access are, all else equal, more likely to be influential.
definitions.quote: While access does not guarantee influence, it is customarily seen as a crucial step towards gaining political influence.

definitions.definition: A group that is offered access but declines the invitation does not count as an instance of access.
definitions.quote: the definition excludes instances where a group is offered access but neglects the invitation.

findings.claim: The authors report that, in the literature they reviewed, the concept of access rests on an intuitive understanding rather than an explicit definition, which hampers methodological discussion of measurement.
findings.quote: the concept of access rests on an intuitive understanding rather than an explicit definition. This hampers methodological discussions of measurement.

limitations.point: Only the abstract, notes and reference list were in the saved page; the article body (pp. 306-321) was not available, so the full definition, its justification and the comparison of operationalisations are not recorded.
limitations.quote: This is a preview of subscription content, log in via an institution to check access.

limitations.point: Access is not necessary for influence: structural position can give influence without lobbying, and the access approach does not capture this.
limitations.quote: Access is not necessary for being influential.

limitations.point: The definition leaves out groups that are offered access but do not take it, even though this may indicate a powerful group.
limitations.quote: This may very well indicate that this group is powerful and important, but it will not count as an instance of access according to our definition.

Candidates for the library.
